This is one of the causes why many pleasures, which we cultivate with all our might, cannot be immortal. If a person be thirsty, spring water is nectar to him ; if hungry, any kind of food is agreeable, even the smell of food is grateful. To a man in a heat, or in a fever, cold is pleasing ; and to one in a cold fit nothing is so agreeable as heat.
